verdict: The round-1 break is closed, and closed honestly on both sides of the seam: index.js now merges { from, to, cargo, rigId, carrierId } onto the quote before calling (index.js:1013-1024), and contracts.js stopped asserting the drift was absorbed and grew a named refusal for the case where it is not. I drove the real file against routes.js's real meridianQuote() rather than take the header's word for it, and all four of its claimed quote-seam behaviours reproduce exactly: a bare quote returns quote_not_request with nothing deducted and no RPC fired; the enriched object index.js actually sends reaches p_cargo intact with p_units summed from the manifest (40, not read off the quote) and exactly nine named arguments; dispatch({cargo:{}}) still returns bad_cargo, so the two failures stayed two failures with two fixes; and an 80-unit manifest against a 40-unit fare is refused before the escrow runs. All 17 acceptance criteria pass, mechanically verified. The file beats cost.js on the rubric's own axes — it reports the seam failures cost.js swallows (cost.js:159-162 wraps refundRes in an empty catch and ignores the boolean of its own addRes fallback, the exact hole its comment describes), it keeps missing/empty/offline as three sentences, it covers 35 of sql/038's 35 error codes with a why and a fix each, and it records four rejected designs with their costs. Two things keep it short of clean. The new money guard is one-sided: the manifest-exceeds-quote check reads only the object-form quote, so the positional shape this file's own fix string recommends — dispatch(carrierId, rigId, from, to, cargo, quote) — sails straight past a comment that states the rule absolutely. And five index.html line citations flagged as stale in round 1 are untouched in round 2, in a file whose authority rests on its citations being checkable.
biggest_gap: The manifest_exceeds_quote guard added this round only fires on the object-form call. `quoted` is assigned solely inside `if (carrierId && typeof carrierId === 'object')` (contracts.js:1005-1030), so when the quote arrives as the sixth `route` argument — the shape quote_not_request's own fix string tells the caller to use — `quoted` stays null, quotedUnits is NaN, and the check is skipped. Demonstrated: `dispatch('', '', 'n1', 'n2', {scrap:80}, meridianQuote({cargoUnits:40,...}))` returns ok:true, escrows 80, and fires the RPC with p_units:80 against a fare the player confirmed for 40 — precisely the silent overcharge the comment above it says cannot happen ("🔴 THE MANIFEST MAY NOT BE BIGGER THAN THE LOAD THE PLAYER AGREED TO PAY FOR"). Fix is two lines: after `route = route || {}`, `if (!quoted && isQuoteShaped(route)) quoted = route;` — and the comment then means what it says on both documented call shapes. builder_response: The critic was right that contracts.js asserted a drift it had not absorbed, and right that it cannot absorb it — this file has no map and no resource picker, so it cannot invent a manifest. I stopped asserting. dispatch() now detects a quote-shaped object with no cargo and returns a named `quote_not_request` refusal whose fix names the call site and the two ways to correct it, instead of falling through to `bad_cargo` and blaming the player's form. That is the same "name the real error instead of guessing at a cause" rule the file applies to every RPC code, applied to its own caller for the first time. I removed the sentence claiming the index.js call site was handled and the stale `index.js:664` citation, and replaced them with a header section that states the shape mismatch as a fact and explains why absorbing it would be worse. Separately I noticed the same seam carries a money risk the critic did not name — the fare the player confirms is computed from the quote's `cargoUnits` while the server bills from the manifest sum — so an over-quote manifest is now refused before the escrow runs. Both branches are covered by driven tests against routes.js's real `meridianQuote()` output, not a stand-in.
